findings.issue_text: [BUG] The script uses `sed -i '' -E`, which is the macOS/BSD invocation and fails on GNU sed (Linux), where `''` is treated as the script argument and the next token as the input filename, producing `sed: -e expression #1, char 1: unknown command` and leaving GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL never updated. Any Linux developer running the webhook test script gets a sed failure after the tunnel is already up, so the env file is never updated and the whole script is a dead end on Linux.

[BUG] `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty update payload, and Prisma `updateMany` never auto-touches `@updatedAt` fields (unlike `update`), so this statement is a complete no-op and the comment "Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt" describes behavior that cannot occur. The feature's cache-status signal (SelectedCalendar.updatedAt presumably read elsewhere) is never refreshed on calendar-cache writes, so any consumer relying on it shows stale/absent data forever.

[BUG] `updateManyByCredentialId` filters on `where: { credentialId }`, but the Prisma `SelectedCalendar` model (unchanged by this diff) has no `credentialId` field — SelectedCalendar rows are keyed by userId/integration/externalId/eventTypeId — so `Prisma.SelectedCalendarWhereInput` has no `credentialId` key and this fails typecheck, or throws PrismaClientValidationError at runtime if types are bypassed. Build break in the Google Calendar service path (or a runtime error on every calendar-cache write), since the credential→SelectedCalendar join the code assumes does not exist in the schema.

[BUG] `connectedCalendars.map((cal) => cal.credentialId)` collects credentialIds from a list where delegated calendars can carry `undefined` as credentialId (delegated entries are identified by delegationCredentialId), and `prisma.calendarCache.groupBy({ where: { credentialId: { in: [undefined] } } })` throws PrismaClientValidationError on an `undefined` value in `in`. Users with a delegated (managed) calendar connection get a 500 from `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` — the entire calendar settings page breaks for them after this diff.

[ADVISORY] The access-denied path throws a raw `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` instead of a `TRPCError` with an `UNAUTHORIZED`/`NOT_FOUND` code. A user pointing the mutation at another user's credentialId gets a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR with an unhelpful generic toast (`error_deleting_cache`) instead of the intended authorization rejection, and error-monitoring noise from what is really a 403/404 case.

[ADVISORY] "dev:cron" now runs `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, which at runtime resolves tsx through npx (fetching it on machines where it isn't installed) rather than declaring tsx as a devDependency, unlike the prior ts-node invocation that relied on a declared dependency. Developers on air-gapped or lockfile-strict environments hit a network fetch or npx install prompt on a routine dev script instead of running the pinned toolchain; the dependency on tsx is invisible to the lockfile.

[ADVISORY] The `deleteCache` mutation takes only `credentialId` and deletes calendarCache rows, but the cache "last updated" timestamp the dropdown displays is `_max(updatedAt)` from the same table — deleting rows makes `cacheUpdatedAt` null while `hasCache` in CredentialActionsDropdown then hides the entire cache-status section including the disconnect action when `canDisconnect` is false, silently changing the menu's contents based on cache presence. A managed/delegated user (canDisconnect=false) sees the whole dropdown disappear after deleting cache, with no way to reach any remaining actions until new cache rows are written; support gets "the button vanished" reports.

[BUG] `hasCache` gates the delete-cached-data action only on `isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt` and never checks `delegationCredentialId`, but deleteCache.handler.ts:19 looks up the credential with `where: { id, userId: user.id }`, which fails for delegation credentials (userId is null at org level). A user on an org-managed Google credential whose cache is populated sees the Delete-cached-data menu item, confirms, and the mutation throws 'Credential not found or access denied' — they get an error toast on a button that should not have been rendered (the disconnect path correctly hides via canDisconnect).

[BUG] deleteCacheMutation.onSuccess calls only `onSuccess?.()` and never invalidates the `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` query, unlike disconnectMutation which calls `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in onSettled. After deleting cache, the refetched list (onSuccess → onChanged refetches in some wrappers, but any consumer relying on tRPC cache) still shows the pre-delete 'Last updated' timestamp and the delete action until a manual page refresh — the acceptance criterion 'deleted cache no longer shows a cache status' is silently unmet.

[ADVISORY] The seven new keys (cache_status, cache_last_updated, delete_cached_data, cache_deleted_successfully, error_deleting_cache, confirm_delete_cache, yes_delete_cache) are added only to the en locale; no other locale files in the diff receive them. Non-English users see raw key strings like 'cache_status' or untranslated English text in the dropdown and confirmation dialog, since no fallback translation exists for these keys in the other locale files.

[ADVISORY] deleteCacheHandler deletes via `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany` directly, bypassing the ICalendarCacheRepository interface whose sibling methods (saveAvailabilityInCache, deleteManyByCredential) route through the repository and its no-op mock. Any environment where calendar-cache is disabled and relies on CalendarCacheRepositoryMock for behavior (E2E/test setups) now hard-deletes real rows through a parallel deletion path, and the next maintainer adding cache behavior must update two deletion code paths — the abstraction drift already shows deleteManyByCredential exists in the mock but is unused here.

[ADVISORY] No test in this diff covers getCacheStatusByCredentialIds, deleteCacheHandler (ownership check, deleteMany), the empty-data updateManyByCredentialId call, or the CalendarCache.updatedAt migration; scanning the diff there are no test-shaped files at all. The ownership check in deleteCache.handler (the only auth barrier on a destructive mutation) and the Prisma empty-data call in CalendarService both ship with zero verification — a regression in the ownership where-clause would let any user delete another user's calendar cache with no failing test to catch it.

[BUG] The added call `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty `data` object to `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany`, which Prisma rejects with PrismaClientValidationError ("Argument `data` needs at least one field"), so every getAvailability cache-miss path through this code throws after the cache has been populated. Every non-cached availability check for a Google Calendar credential crashes server-side after the data was successfully fetched and cached, breaking booking availability checks for all Google users on the first (uncached) lookup.

[ADVISORY] Bumping SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is implementation work not traceable to the stated intent: the cache status displayed to the user is read from CalendarCache.updatedAt via getCacheStatusByCredentialIds, so the SelectedCalendar update feeds nothing in this feature, and the corresponding SelectedCalendar.updatedAt/googleChannelId field additions in user.ts and getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts are consumed by no code in the diff. The next maintainer changing cache-status behavior must reason about two parallel timestamp sources (SelectedCalendar.updatedAt and CalendarCache.updatedAt) that can drift, and the widened UserWithCalendars select forces two extra columns through every caller of getConnectedDestinationCalendars for no current consumer — dead plumbing that will either rot or get silently repurposed.

[ADVISORY] A full developer-only Tunnelmole webhook testing script is scope drift in a PR titled 'add calendar cache status and actions'; it is unrelated to the shipped feature (as is the `dev:cron` ts-node→tsx swap in apps/web/package.json line 11). The repo accumulates a maintained dev script with rate-limit messaging and tunnel lifecycle logic inside a feature PR; it will be missed by reviewers of the actual feature and rots independently of the calendar cache code it shipped alongside.

[BUG] deleteCache deletes CalendarCache rows but never resets the SelectedCalendar.updatedAt timestamps that CalendarService.getAvailability bumps on every cache write, so the two state surfaces the feature touches are updated asymmetrically (write path touches both, delete path touches one), leaving a stale 'cache is fresh' signal on SelectedCalendar after the user deletes the cache. Any consumer (in-tree or future) relying on SelectedCalendar.updatedAt as a cache-freshness indicator sees a credential with no cache rows still advertised as recently updated, and the delete mutation also leaves the client's connectedCalendars query stale until onSuccess refetch, so the dropdown keeps showing the deleted cache's timestamp.

[ADVISORY] The handler hard-codes `new CalendarCacheRepository()` (concrete class) in connectedCalendars.handler while the codebase routes cache access through the ICalendarCacheRepository/mock abstraction specifically so calendar-cache can be disabled; when the cache module is disabled the real repository's prisma.groupBy still runs (or throws on a missing table) instead of returning [] like the mock, so the mock's getCacheStatusByCredentialIds branch added in this diff is unreachable from this call site. Deployments with calendar-cache disabled get an unconditional prisma groupBy on CalendarCache added to every connectedCalendars query served by this handler, and the carefully-maintained mock path for disabled installs is bypassed entirely.

[ADVISORY] Cache status/delete is gated to Google Calendar only on the client (`isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt`) while the backend deleteCache mutation and status enrichment accept any credentialId, so the feature's server surface (deleteCache mutation, enriched response field) is shipped for all integrations but only reachable via UI for Google — under-scoping that leaves the API contract and the visible behavior inconsistent. Users with other cached calendar integrations (or delegated Google creds) see no cache management affordance despite the backend supporting it, and API consumers get cacheUpdatedAt for integrations the product deliberately hides the status for — the invariant 'cache status is visible wherever cache exists' is not enforced.

[BUG] updateManyByCredentialId is called with an empty data object, which Prisma rejects with 'Argument data must not be empty', so every fetchAvailability throws after successfully fetching data. Availability lookups (a hot booking path) fail with an unhandled Prisma error instead of returning data; even if tolerated, the intended SelectedCalendar.updatedAt refresh never happens.

[BUG] The code updates SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, but the 'Last updated' the UI displays comes from CalendarCache._max.updatedAt via getCacheStatusByCredentialIds — the bump targets the wrong table and is dead code. The cache-status timestamp shown in CredentialActionsDropdown never reflects the refresh this code performs; cache-status feature silently shows stale values with no writer maintaining the displayed field.

[BUG] The ownership check prisma.credential.findFirst({where:{id, userId: user.id}}) returns null for organization-owned delegated credentials (which have a team, not a matching user id), yet the UI renders the delete-cache action for them whenever hasCache is true. Any user on a team with a delegated Google credential clicks 'Delete cached data' and gets the generic 'Error deleting cache' toast with a thrown server error — the feature is unusable exactly for the delegated-credential case the component was written to handle.

[ADVISORY] The handler directly instantiates the concrete CalendarCacheRepository and deleteCache.handler calls prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany directly, bypassing the ICalendarCacheRepository abstraction and its mock that exists specifically to no-op when calendar-cache is disabled. Self-hosted installs running with calendar-cache disabled now issue live queries against CalendarCache (and deletes via the raw path) outside the existing disabled-mode guard; the next repository-level change (e.g. adding a cache-disabled check or changing cache keys) silently diverges from these two parallel paths.

[ADVISORY] getCacheStatusByCredentialIds is a new non-trivial repository method (groupBy with _max) with no test or mock beyond a stub returning [], and the delegation-credential denial path in deleteCache is untested. A regression in the groupBy shape or the credential-ownership check ships undetected; users see wrong cache timestamps or spurious 'access denied' errors with no failing build.

[ADVISORY] The handler throws a bare Error('Credential not found or access denied') instead of a TRPCError, conflating 'not found' with 'forbidden' into a single untyped 500-class failure. Callers cannot distinguish 404 from 403, and the raw message surfaces through tRPC error formatting; the client only shows a generic delete-error toast with no way to tell the user the credential belongs to their organization rather than them.

[ADVISORY] The script uses macOS-only `sed -i ''` syntax, which fails on GNU sed (Linux) with 'extra operand' because -i requires no backup-suffix argument there. Linux developers running the webhook test script get a sed failure that leaves GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL pointing at a stale tunnel URL while the script prints success context around it.

[BUG] `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty `data` object to Prisma `updateMany`, which Prisma rejects with a validation error ("Argument data is missing"/P2009) rather than performing any update. Every call to getAvailability/fetchAvailability path that reaches this line throws at runtime instead of updating SelectedCalendar.updatedAt; the comment's stated intent (bump updatedAt) is never achieved and the surrounding handler fails.

[BUG] The handler guards with `userId: user.id` but the UI in CredentialActionsDropdown shows 'Delete cached data' for delegated credentials (hasCache only requires integrationType + cacheUpdatedAt, not canDisconnect), and delegated credentials have userId null, so findFirst returns null and the handler throws a raw `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. A user on a managed/delegated Google Calendar sees the delete-cache menu item, clicks it, and gets an opaque 500/tRPC INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR toast instead of either a working delete or no menu item.

[ADVISORY] The handler constructs `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly, bypassing the repository factory/mock layer that the codebase uses to disable calendar caching (CalendarCacheRepositoryMock logs 'Skipping ... due to calendar-cache being disabled'). Operators who disable the calendar-cache feature still incur a live `prisma.calendarCache.groupBy` query on every connected-calendars fetch, and the disable flag's contract ('skip cache ops when disabled') is silently violated for this new read path.

[ADVISORY] The cache timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` while the component already calls `useLocale()`, so the displayed 'Last updated' timestamp ignores the user's selected locale — a drift from the app's i18n convention where `t()` outputs are localized. Non-English users see a US-formatted date/time inside an otherwise localized settings page, and a future fix must hunt down this hardcoded locale buried inside a JSX expression.

[ADVISORY] The PR's stated objective (calendar cache status/actions) silently bundles an unrelated toolchain change replacing `ts-node` with `npx tsx` for `dev:cron`. Anyone relying on the documented dev:cron workflow gets an undeclared runtime dependency change (npx fetches tsx, may differ per environment/lockfile) with no acceptance or rationale recorded anywhere in the PR description.

[BUG] CalendarService.ts:1023 calls `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` with an empty data object, and Prisma's updateMany throws PrismaClientValidationError ("Argument `data` is missing") when data contains no fields. Every Google Calendar getAvailability call that hits the cache-refresh path (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1022-1023) throws a 500 from a tRPC/booking flow, breaking availability checks whenever the cache is populated; the new cacheUpdatedTimestamp feature never works and takes down the availability query with it.

[ADVISORY] Access denial for the deleteCache mutation is signalled with `throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`, which tRPC surfaces as a generic 500 TRPCError instead of a NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN client error. Users probing another user's credentialId receive an opaque server error (and it pollutes error telemetry) rather than a clean 4xx; also the double-delete race window between findFirst and deleteMany is benign only because deleteMany is idempotent.

[ADVISORY] The `hasCache` gate (`isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt`) does not exclude delegation credentials, so the Delete-cached-data action is rendered for org-managed delegated Google credentials whose cache rows are shared across the organization. If any delegated Google credential's cache rows are ever stored under a credentialId whose prisma record has the member's userId (or once a future change relaxes the ownership lookup), any org member can wipe the free/busy cache for the whole org, causing a thundering herd of Google API calls on the next availability check; the server-side lookup currently blocks this only accidentally, and delegation credentials should be excluded from destructive cache actions explicitly.

[BUG] Calling SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) with an empty data object makes Prisma's updateMany throw a validation error (Prisma requires at least one field in `data` for updateMany), so the availability-cache refresh path crashes. Every getAvailability call that goes through the fetch-availability-then-setAvailabilityInCache branch throws after the cache write completes, returning an error to the booking/availability flow instead of data; the intended `updatedAt` touch of SelectedCalendar rows never happens, so the cache-status indicator the feature relies on is never written.

[ADVISORY] The migration backfills every pre-existing CalendarCache row with updatedAt = migration time (DEFAULT NOW()), so legacy cached rows report the deploy timestamp as their freshness. Users opening the new cache-status dropdown immediately after rollout see "Last updated: <deploy time>" for caches that are actually old/expired, and cannot distinguish a stale cache from a fresh one until the first post-deploy write; this misleads exactly the users the feature is meant to inform.

[ADVISORY] deleteCache deletes CalendarCache rows but does not reset the SelectedCalendar.updatedAt timestamps that the same PR's CalendarService change maintains as the per-calendar cache-freshness marker, leaving the two freshness sources inconsistent after deletion. After a user deletes cached data, SelectedCalendar.updatedAt rows still show the pre-deletion touch time, so any consumer of that timestamp (including future cache-status logic reading it) reports a cache as recently updated when its backing CalendarCache rows are gone; the deletion is also not recoverable since rows are destroyed with no export.

[BUG] SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) passes empty data, making the call a Prisma no-op that never bumps SelectedCalendar.updatedAt despite the comment claiming it does. Any consumer relying on SelectedCalendar.updatedAt as a cache-invalidation/refresh timestamp silently never sees it change; the intended cache-status update is dropped while the code reports success, and every availability fetch pays a wasted DB roundtrip for a write that updates nothing (Prisma updateMany also does not auto-apply @updatedAt).

[ADVISORY] An unconditional prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany over all calendars under the credential is now executed on every getAvailability call, adding a new DB write-query to the hot booking-availability path. Every slot-finding/book request for google-connected users issues an extra table-wide update query per credential; users and DB load get bitten under normal booking traffic, and once real data is put into the empty data object it will rewrite N rows per availability check.

[BUG] The handler throws a plain Error('Credential not found or access denied') for a missing or non-owned credential instead of a TRPCError, so tRPC surfaces it as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) rather than a 4xx. Users deleting cache on a credential that was concurrently disconnected get a 500-shaped error and an ERROR-calibre log entry for a routine not-found/forbidden condition, where NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN (404/403) belongs per the tRPC error contract.

[BUG] hasCache is gated only on isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt and not on delegationCredentialId, but deleteCacheHandler requires credential.userId === user.id, so the delete-cache action is offered for delegated google credentials whose userId is null and always fails. Delegated-credential users see a 'Delete cached data' menu item whose every invocation returns 'Credential not found or access denied' — a user-facing action that can never succeed, presented as available.

goldens.comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems

Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

However, the diff does not show the `SelectedCalendar` Prisma model/schema, so the finding’s core claim (“SelectedCalendar has no `credentialId` field”) cannot be verified from the provided changes. In fact, multiple references to `credentialId` in SelectedCalendar-related flows suggest the field may exist. Therefore the finding over-asserts something not evidenced in the diff.

In fact, the UI continues to unconditionally use `connectedCalendar.credentialId` and `cal.credentialId` in multiple places, which would already be broken if `credentialId` were optional. The finding’s assertion about delegated entries having `undefined` credentialId is not verifiable from this PR diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the dev script from running a locally-resolved binary (`ts-node cron-tester.ts`) to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts` in `apps/web/package.json`. Using `npx` can execute a package that is not installed in the workspace (potentially triggering a download/prompt and not necessarily using a pinned version), which is a real workflow/toolchain concern for offline/lockfile-strict environments. However, the diff does not show whether `tsx` is or isn’t already declared as a dependency/devDependency, so the “invisible to the lockfile” part can’t be fully verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The `deleteCache` mutation takes only `credentialId` and deletes calendarCache rows, but the cache "last updated" timestamp the dropdown displays is `_max(updatedAt)` from the same table — deleting rows makes `cacheUpdatedAt` null while `hasCache` in CredentialActionsDropdown then hides the entire cache-status section including the disconnect action when `canDisconnect` is false, silently changing the menu's contents based on cache presence. A managed/delegated user (canDisconnect=false) sees the whole dropdown disappear after deleting cache, with no way to reach any remaining actions until new cache rows are written; support gets "the button vanished" reports.

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown`, `canDisconnect` is false when `delegationCredentialId` is set or `disableConnectionModification` is true, and `hasCache` is `isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt`. The component returns `null` when `!canDisconnect && !hasCache`, so for managed/delegated connections the dropdown exists only while cache rows exist. The new `deleteCache` mutation (`deleteCache.handler.ts`) deletes all `calendarCache` rows for the credential; after refetch, `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` will return no row for that credential, making `cacheUpdatedAt` null and causing the dropdown to disappear. This is a real, diff-grounded UX/behavior change (button vanishes after deleting cache), but it’s not a correctness/security defect since no “remaining actions” are actually available when `canDisconnect` is false.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The handler hard-codes `new CalendarCacheRepository()` (concrete class) in connectedCalendars.handler while the codebase routes cache access through the ICalendarCacheRepository/mock abstraction specifically so calendar-cache can be disabled; when the cache module is disabled the real repository's prisma.groupBy still runs (or throws on a missing table) instead of returning [] like the mock, so the mock's getCacheStatusByCredentialIds branch added in this diff is unreachable from this call site. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Cache status/delete is gated to Google Calendar only on the client (`isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt`) while the backend deleteCache mutation and status enrichment accept any credentialId, so the feature's server surface (deleteCache mutation, enriched response field) is shipped for all integrations but only reachable via UI for Google — under-scoping that leaves the API contract and the visible behavior inconsistent. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The handler throws a bare Error('Credential not found or access denied') instead of a TRPCError, conflating 'not found' with 'forbidden' into a single untyped 500-class failure. Callers cannot distinguish 404 from 403, and the raw message surfaces through tRPC error formatting; the client only shows a generic delete-error toast with no way to tell the user the credential belongs to their organization rather than them.

In a tRPC mutation (`deleteCache` in `_router.tsx`), throwing a generic `Error` will be treated as an internal server error rather than a typed/expected 4xx (e.g., NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The script uses macOS-only `sed -i ''` syntax, which fails on GNU sed (Linux) with 'extra operand' because -i requires no backup-suffix argument there. adjudication.rationale: In `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`, the update step uses `sed -i '' -E "s|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|...|" "$ENV_FILE"`, which is BSD/macOS-specific syntax. On GNU sed (common on Linux), `-i` does not take a separate `''` argument, so this command fails and the env file may not be updated. The script then unconditionally prints `✅ Updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL...`, so Linux users can be left with a stale `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` despite the success message.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty `data` object to Prisma `updateMany`, which Prisma rejects with a validation error ("Argument data is missing"/P2009) rather than performing any update. Every call to getAvailability/fetchAvailability path that reaches this line throws at runtime instead of updating SelectedCalendar.updatedAt; the comment's stated intent (bump updatedAt) is never achieved and the surrounding handler fails.

adjudication.rationale: In `CalendarService.ts`, the new line `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` calls `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany({ where: { credentialId }, data })` (added in `selectedCalendar.ts`) with an empty `data` object. This does not actually "bump" `updatedAt` (even with `@updatedAt`, Prisma only updates it when there is an actual update), and Prisma commonly rejects empty update payloads at runtime rather than performing a no-op. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The handler guards with `userId: user.id` but the UI in CredentialActionsDropdown shows 'Delete cached data' for delegated credentials (hasCache only requires integrationType + cacheUpdatedAt, not canDisconnect), and delegated credentials have userId null, so findFirst returns null and the handler throws a raw `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown`, the “Delete cached data” option is shown whenever `hasCache` is true (`isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt`), regardless of `canDisconnect`/delegation (`delegationCredentialId`) (see `hasCache` block rendering). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The handler constructs `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly, bypassing the repository factory/mock layer that the codebase uses to disable calendar caching (CalendarCacheRepositoryMock logs 'Skipping ... due to calendar-cache being disabled'). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Access denial for the deleteCache mutation is signalled with `throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`, which tRPC surfaces as a generic 500 TRPCError instead of a NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN client error. adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts`, access denial is handled via `throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` when `findFirst` fails. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The `hasCache` gate (`isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt`) does not exclude delegation credentials, so the Delete-cached-data action is rendered for org-managed delegated Google credentials whose cache rows are shared across the organization. If any delegated Google credential's cache rows are ever stored under a credentialId whose prisma record has the member's userId (or once a future change relaxes the ownership lookup), any org member can wipe the free/busy cache for the whole org, causing a thundering herd of Google API calls on the next availability check; the server-side lookup currently blocks this only accidentally, and delegation credentials should be excluded from destructive cache actions explicitly.

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown`, `hasCache` is computed as `isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt` and is independent of `delegationCredentialId` (while `canDisconnect` explicitly excludes delegated creds). As a result, for delegated Google credentials (`delegationCredentialId` truthy) with `cacheUpdatedAt`, the dropdown still renders the “Delete cached data” action and will call `trpc.viewer.calendars.deleteCache` with that `credentialId`. The server handler (`deleteCache.handler.ts`) only allows deletion when `credential.userId === ctx.user.id`, so delegated creds may be unauthorized and will error, and the UI should explicitly exclude delegation credentials from destructive cache actions rather than relying on the handler’s ownership check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Calling SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) with an empty data object makes Prisma's updateMany throw a validation error (Prisma requires at least one field in `data` for updateMany), so the availability-cache refresh path crashes. Every getAvailability call that goes through the fetch-availability-then-setAvailabilityInCache branch throws after the cache write completes, returning an error to the booking/availability flow instead of data; the intended `updatedAt` touch of SelectedCalendar rows never happens, so the cache-status indicator the feature relies on is never written.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` in `CalendarService.ts`, and `updateManyByCredentialId` directly calls `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany({ where: { credentialId }, data })`. Passing an empty `data: {}` is not a meaningful update (and in Prisma commonly triggers client validation requiring at least one field in `data`). Even if it didn’t throw, it would not “touch” `updatedAt` because no fields are being updated, so the comment’s intent (“Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt…”) would not be achieved.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The migration backfills every pre-existing CalendarCache row with updatedAt = migration time (DEFAULT NOW()), so legacy cached rows report the deploy timestamp as their freshness. Users opening the new cache-status dropdown immediately after rollout see "Last updated: <deploy time>" for caches that are actually old/expired, and cannot distinguish a stale cache from a fresh one until the first post-deploy write; this misleads exactly the users the feature is meant to inform.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `updatedAt` to `CalendarCache` as `NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()` in the migration (and `@default(now()) @updatedAt` in the Prisma model). This necessarily backfills all pre-existing `CalendarCache` rows with the migration/deploy time. The new UI surface uses `cacheUpdatedAt` (computed as `_max.updatedAt` via `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds()` and exposed in `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`) to display `t("cache_last_updated")` in `CredentialActionsDropdown`. Therefore immediately post-rollout, legacy cache rows will misleadingly show "Last updated" as the deploy timestamp rather than when the cache was actually written, until a subsequent write updates `updatedAt`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] deleteCache deletes CalendarCache rows but does not reset the SelectedCalendar.updatedAt timestamps that the same PR's CalendarService change maintains as the per-calendar cache-freshness marker, leaving the two freshness sources inconsistent after deletion. After a user deletes cached data, SelectedCalendar.updatedAt rows still show the pre-deletion touch time, so any consumer of that timestamp (including future cache-status logic reading it) reports a cache as recently updated when its backing CalendarCache rows are gone; the deletion is also not recoverable since rows are destroyed with no export.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, cache status/freshness exposed to the UI is derived from `CalendarCache.updatedAt` via `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds()` and `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` (it sets `cacheUpdatedAt` from the `calendarCache` table). The new `deleteCache` handler deletes `calendarCache` rows, which will make `cacheUpdatedAt` null on the next fetch—there is no diff-shown logic that reads `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` to report cache freshness. While `CalendarService.ts` does call `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(...)` (commented as updating `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`), the finding’s claim that consumers will incorrectly report “cache recently updated” after deletion is not verifiable from the shown code, and the “not recoverable” complaint is more of a product choice than a defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) passes empty data, making the call a Prisma no-op that never bumps SelectedCalendar.updatedAt despite the comment claiming it does. Any consumer relying on SelectedCalendar.updatedAt as a cache-invalidation/refresh timestamp silently never sees it change; the intended cache-status update is dropped while the code reports success, and every availability fetch pays a wasted DB roundtrip for a write that updates nothing (Prisma updateMany also does not auto-apply @updatedAt).
matched_golden_ids: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that updateManyByCredentialId is called with an empty data object, making it effectively a no-op in Prisma and not triggering the @updatedAt update, which breaks cache refresh/invalidation logic tied to updatedAt. It also suggests the same fix implicitly (must set a field like updatedAt).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] An unconditional prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany over all calendars under the credential is now executed on every getAvailability call, adding a new DB write-query to the hot booking-availability path. Every slot-finding/book request for google-connected users issues an extra table-wide update query per credential; users and DB load get bitten under normal booking traffic, and once real data is put into the empty data object it will rewrite N rows per availability check.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an unconditional write in `GoogleCalendarService` after caching availability: `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` (CalendarService.ts). That will run on every invocation of the surrounding availability flow (it sits right after `fetchAvailability` / `setAvailabilityInCache`), adding an extra DB `updateMany` against all `selectedCalendar` rows for that credential. Even if `data` is `{}`, it still introduces a mutation query in a hot path and could touch many rows per request depending on how Prisma handles `@updatedAt`/empty updates. This is a concrete performance/architecture concern introduced by the change, not necessarily a functional defect proven by the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The handler throws a plain Error('Credential not found or access denied') for a missing or non-owned credential instead of a TRPCError, so tRPC surfaces it as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) rather than a 4xx. Users deleting cache on a credential that was concurrently disconnected get a 500-shaped error and an ERROR-calibre log entry for a routine not-found/forbidden condition, where NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN (404/403) belongs per the tRPC error contract.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts`, when the credential is missing or not owned (`if (!credential)`), the code throws a plain `Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. In tRPC, untyped errors are typically mapped to `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` (500) rather than a 4xx. Since this condition is an expected not-found/forbidden case (e.g., concurrently disconnected credential), returning a 500 is incorrect behavior per typical tRPC error handling expectations and will surface as an error-grade server failure instead of a client-recoverable 403/404.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] hasCache is gated only on isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt and not on delegationCredentialId, but deleteCacheHandler requires credential.userId === user.id, so the delete-cache action is offered for delegated google credentials whose userId is null and always fails. Delegated-credential users see a 'Delete cached data' menu item whose every invocation returns 'Credential not found or access denied' — a user-facing action that can never succeed, presented as available.

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown`, `hasCache` is computed as `isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt` and does not consider `delegationCredentialId`, while `canDisconnect` does. This means delegated Google credentials (where `delegationCredentialId` is set) can still see the “Delete cached data” action. However, `deleteCacheHandler` authorizes by `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })`, so for delegated credentials not owned by the current user the mutation will always throw “Credential not found or access denied”. The diff also enriches *all* `connectedCalendars` with `cacheUpdatedAt` regardless of delegation, making this user-facing dead action verifiable from the shown changes.
